product_commit_scope: Schema-2 tool source exercised by the parent in the development container under the shared heavy-work lock; not an actual Shenko long-run result.
what_it_is: A stdlib-only Linux observation tool. Schema 2 binds one directory/run to an intact matching header and manifest, requires gap-free samples and same-boot uptime corroboration, refuses damaged-log continuation, and associates restart boundaries with samples. Verification below is bounded native procfs plus labeled synthetic evidence copies, not long-run stability.
what_it_proves: Nine permanent scenarios passed and documentation integrity reported no errors.
Actual short-lived procfs sampling retained real boot/process identity and correctly left 7/30-day windows unobserved with require-observed exit 3.
The external consumer passed 44 assertions over real process observations and explicitly synthetic gap/header/torn-tail/boundary-retry copies; original captured bytes were retained.
source_repairs: Known sampler gaps disqualify every declared window; endpoint span is diagnostic only. Uptime corroboration prevents a wall-clock step from manufacturing elapsed coverage; discontinuous or unverifiable clocks do not qualify.

One first matching schema/header/run/manifest/recorder binding is required. Missing headers, drift, foreign runs, unknown or malformed records, missing/duplicate sample sequences and unverifiable live-process identities do not qualify.
Any unterminated tail, including parseable JSON without its newline, is refused before another append; damaged bytes remain unchanged.
Kernel boot ID comes from /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id. PID changes are classified before same-PID starttime changes; zombie/dead processes do not count as alive or accumulate live-process uptime.

Restart boundaries carry sample_seq. A complete boundary followed by a failed sample write is reused on retry, and reports count only unique sample-corroborated transitions. Unmatched boundaries remain integrity gaps.
Acknowledged appends fsync both file and containing directory, including newly created log entries and retries.
The permanent suite now contains exactly 9 independent scenarios. Redundant old cases were removed rather than regrouped. Schema-1 evidence is retained as bytes, not inferred into the new format.
scenario_inventory: known sampling gap across a thirty-day endpoint span
torn append refusal with byte preservation
one PID replacement with a failed sample write and retry

historical_execution.scope_correction: The old four function names concealed at least ten independent behaviors. Those reported passes do not validate the repaired source, prove the nine reviewed properties, or establish physical durability.

what_it_does_not_prove: The observed subject was a controlled sleep process, not the Shenko model-driven subject.
No 7-day or 30-day run has been performed or observed; no candidate long-run data exists.
No RSS/drift/uptime/failure-distribution numbers for any Shenko candidate.
No router/Android/multi-node profiles, physical power-loss RPO, or subject behavioral correctness (continuous thinking or no message loss).
Samples are points in time. Between-sample behavior is not proven; restarts require the actual new PID. Cross-boot continuity is conservatively rejected.
One writer per run is required. Local evidence is unsigned and candidate metadata is caller-supplied; the sampler does not attest that a PID executed the declared binary.
